A 36-year-old male seeks medical attention from his primary care physician due to concentration
difficulties. He has lived with his parents throughout his life and recently secured employment at a local
factory. Since starting work, he struggles to maintain focus on tasks, and his supervisor frequently
notices him "daydreaming" with a vacant stare, requiring loud verbal prompts to regain his attention.
The patient reports constant fatigue and occasional sudden sleep episodes while operating machinery.
Despite attempting earlier bedtimes for the past month, he can only fall asleep two hours before his
alarm. His vital signs show: temperature 97.7°F (37°C), blood pressure 117/66 mmHg, pulse 73/min,
and respirations 15/min. Physical examination reveals no abnormalities. The patient is concerned
about potential job loss. What is the most appropriate first step in management? Answer Choices: (A)
Referral to a neurologist for epilepsy evaluation (B) Modafinil (C) Continuous positive airway pressure
(CPAP) therapy (D) Polysomnography (E) Bright light therapy and decreased light at night (F) Initiation
of a stimulant such as methylphenidate (G) Cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia (H) Melatonin
supplementation (I) Sleep restriction therapy (J) Ethosuximide
 A. Initiation of a stimulant such as methylphenidate
B. Ethosuximide
C. Melatonin supplementation
D. Cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia
E. Referral to a neurologist for epilepsy evaluation
